builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
summary: RIPPLE replaces prompting-time critique loops and critic-based recovery with a single policy trained via prefix-only teacher distillation plus reinforcement learning that assigns stage-specific credit to reflection, diagnosis, and corrective action. Adoption costs a full training pipeline: teacher supervision, distillation, and RL with local validity gating, which exceeds a 24 GB GPU budget for the model scales typical of repository-level coding agents. Recovery gains concentrate only where the prefix contains sufficient diagnostic evidence and the repository state remains reversible, so the policy can still fail to recover under evidence-poor failures or irreversible states.
rationale: The method requires a distillation-plus-RL training workflow that constrained infrastructure cannot support, so the reader should track it rather than adopt or test it now.
technique: Process-level recovery training with stage-aware credit

claims.statement: RIPPLE replaces prompting-time critique loops and critic-based recovery with a single policy trained via prefix-only teacher distillation plus reinforcement learning that assigns stage-specific credit to reflection, diagnosis, and corrective action. Adoption costs a full training pipeline: teacher supervision, distillation, and RL with local validity gating, which exceeds a 24 GB GPU budget for the model scales typical of repository-level coding agents. Recovery gains concentrate only where the prefix contains sufficient diagnostic evidence and the repository state remains reversible, so the policy can still fail to recover under evidence-poor failures or irreversible states.
Improves the base policy by an arithmetic mean of 4.8 score points across four repository-level software-engineering benchmarks, with no auxiliary critic at deployment.
